lines.name: Closed Ruy Lopez
lines.intro: The main line of the Ruy Lopez. Your bishop pressures the knight that defends e5, and you build slowly with Re1, c3 and h3 before pushing d4.

notes.0: Grab the center and open lines for the queen and the f1 bishop.
notes.1: Black mirrors you and claims an equal share of the center.
notes.2: Develop with tempo: the knight attacks e5.
notes.3: Black defends e5 with the knight.
notes.4: The Ruy Lopez: the bishop hits the knight that defends e5, building long-term pressure.
notes.5: Black asks the bishop right away whether it wants to trade or retreat.
notes.6: Keep the pressure on the knight by stepping back to a4.
notes.7: Black develops and attacks your e4 pawn.
notes.8: Castle. If Black takes on e4, d4 and Re1 win the pawn back with a strong game.
notes.9: Black chooses the solid Closed setup and gets ready to castle.
notes.10: Re1 protects e4, so now Bxc6 followed by Nxe5 becomes a real threat.
notes.11: Black kicks the bishop to get rid of that threat.
notes.12: The bishop settles on b3, aiming at f7.
notes.14: c3 prepares d4 and gives the bishop a retreat square on c2.
notes.16: h3 stops ...Bg4 pinning your knight, so d4 can come next.

lines.name: Berlin Defense
lines.intro: The Berlin is Black's most solid answer. Black grabs e4 and steers into an early queen trade. You end up with the better pawn majority, and Black's king loses the right to castle.

notes.0: Grab the center and open lines for the queen and the f1 bishop.
notes.1: Black mirrors you and claims an equal share of the center.
notes.2: Develop with tempo: the knight attacks e5.
notes.3: Black defends e5 with the knight.
notes.4: The Ruy Lopez: the bishop hits the knight that defends e5, building long-term pressure.
notes.5: The Berlin: Black ignores the bishop and attacks e4.
notes.6: Castle anyway. Black can take e4, but you get it back.
notes.8: Hit the center. Black's e5 pawn is attacked and the e4 knight is exposed.
notes.9: The knight retreats and attacks your bishop.
notes.10: Trade the bishop so you can win back the pawn on e5.
notes.11: Black takes back toward the center, opening lines for both bishops.
notes.12: Win the pawn back, attacking the d6 knight.
notes.13: The knight steps away and offers a queen trade.
notes.15: Black's king can't castle now. This is the famous Berlin endgame: you have the healthier kingside majority, Black has the two bishops.

lines.name: Exchange Variation
lines.intro: You give up the bishop for the knight right away to damage Black's pawns. Black gets the two bishops, but in the endgame your healthy kingside majority can make a passed pawn.

notes.0: Grab the center and open lines for the queen and the f1 bishop.
notes.1: Black mirrors you and claims an equal share of the center.
notes.2: Develop with tempo: the knight attacks e5.
notes.3: Black defends e5 with the knight.
notes.4: The Ruy Lopez: the bishop hits the knight that defends e5, building long-term pressure.
notes.5: Black asks the bishop right away whether it wants to trade or retreat.
notes.6: The Exchange: take the knight and double Black's pawns.
notes.7: Black takes back toward the center to open the c8 bishop.
notes.8: Castle. Now Nxe5 really threatens to win a pawn.
notes.9: Black shores up e5 with the f-pawn.
notes.10: Open the center while Black is still undeveloped.
notes.13: Black kicks the knight away from the center.
notes.14: Retreat and offer a queen trade.
notes.16: Take back with the rook. Your four-against-three kingside majority is the long-term plan: Black's doubled c-pawns can't make a passed pawn on the other side.
